text:
The measured training margins are positive in all four datasets, with only small changes after transition evidence:

| Dataset | Raw dot margin | Complete margin | Context coverage | Positive-edge coverage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Movies_and_TV | 8.2084 | 8.2605 | 24.85% | 4.25% |
| Industrial_and_Scientific | 4.3877 | 4.4112 | 24.83% | 2.59% |
| Electronics | 2.1732 | 2.1863 | 23.05% | 1.86% |
| CDs_and_Vinyl | 4.0232 | 4.0468 | 25.57% | 2.93% |

The complete margins use each training user's excluded-fold graph. Their increases over raw margins are approximately 0.0521, 0.0235, 0.0131, and 0.0236, respectively. These describe sampled training separation; they do not establish validation HR@10 improvement or comparable ranking quality across datasets.

Transition coverage is limited. Roughly one quarter of recency-weighted context sources have retained outgoing edges, while only 1.86–4.25% of sampled positive targets have a retained context edge. Context coverage therefore does not imply broad positive-target coverage.

Mean absolute residuals before the learned gate are small: 0.01308, 0.00597, 0.00329, and 0.00589. Deployment-versus-training residual MAEs are 0.00693, 0.00715, 0.00388, and 0.00744. The measured graph distribution shift is thus material relative to residual magnitude: about 53% in Movies_and_TV and 118–126% in the other datasets. Both quantities are measured before gate scaling; they do not directly quantify final-score or ranking changes.

The multiple-other-user-support strata have complete margins of 11.6954, 7.6845, 4.9586, and 6.5289, exceeding their corresponding overall means. However, their counts are only 87, 53, 38, and 60 out of 2,048 positions. These small, selected strata cannot establish a causal benefit from stronger support. Singleton-support measurements are absent, so a singleton-versus-multiple-support comparison is unavailable.

Sampled item-pair cosine means range from 0.0840 to 0.1508, with standard deviations of 0.1769–0.2676. These measurements alone do not establish severe embedding collapse. Each dataset contributes 2,048 supervised positions from at most four batches, and no rows were unresolved. This supports fold assignment within the measured sample, not catalog-wide representativeness.

No explicit implementation mismatch is established by these diagnostics. A reasonable validation experiment is a matched transition-residual ablation, followed by a test of deployment/training graph alignment or gate regularization. These are uncertain recommendations: select changes using the pinned macro validation HR@10, without assuming larger training margins imply improvement. The supplied measurements provide no evidence about review preferences, unavailable metadata, simulator diversity or conformity traits, full-catalog recommendation quality for the twenty simulator users, or held-out test performance.
